item.title: US charges Cuba's Raúl Castro with murder over 1996 downing of two planes
item.description: Cuba's current president says the charges against Castro - including conspiracy to kill US nationals and destruction of aircraft - are a "political manoeuvre".

item.title: Air France and Airbus found guilty of manslaughter over 2009 plane crash
item.description: The companies were found guilty by a French court over an air disaster which killed 228 people.

item.title: China says US should stop 'threats' against Cuba after ex-leader charged
item.description: It comes after the US charged Cuba's ex-leader with murder, the latest move putting pressure on the regime.

item.title: Gonorrhoea and syphilis hit record levels in Europe
item.description: STIs have surged thanks to record cases and gaps in testing and prevention, a health agency reports.

item.title: Dozens of vehicles burnt as Mali jihadists enforce blockade
item.description: Mali is a landlocked country and depends heavily on fuel transported from neighbouring countries.

item.title: Rosenberg: Putin enjoys Xi's Chinese welcome but heads home without pipeline deal
item.description: Russia and China showed they were shoulder-to-shoulder on the world stage, but it became clear there are limits, says the BBC's Russia Editor.

item.title: DR Congo cancels World Cup training camp over Ebola outbreak
item.description: The outbreak, caused by a rare Ebola species, is thought to have caused 139 deaths so far.

item.title: Sierra Leone becomes latest African country to receive deportees from US
item.description: Nine deportees arrive from the US as part of Donald Trump's crackdown on illegal immigration.

item.title: Nvidia's latest record result fails to impress investors
item.description: The chip giant reported more stellar results but its shares fell after-hours as investors wonder if it can keep up its pace of growth amid greater competition.

item.title: Far-right Israeli minister condemned for taunting handcuffed Gaza flotilla activists
item.description: France and Italy are among the countries that have criticised a video showing Itamar Ben-Gvir taunting dozens of activists detained at an Israeli port.
